observations.meaning: Archive-published Rosetta orbiter position at each CONSERT First Science Sequence measurement point, 15468 rows of SC_POS_X/Y/Z in kilometres. This is the orbiter end of each sounding path; the lander end is the paired CN_G_L_FSS product.
limitations: The archive states the frame for these tables only in DATASET.CAT: 'The geometric data, composed of Rosetta and Philae position, velocity and attitude, are provided in the Comet Fixed Frame coordinate system.' The detached label does not repeat it.

The label's own SC_TARGET_POSITION_VECTOR and SC_SUN_POSITION_VECTOR keywords are a different frame from the table columns; DATASET.CAT gives them as Earth Mean Equator and Equinox of J2000, and the level-2 ERRATA.TXT states the label geometry keywords must not be used.
This product is positions only. The CONSERT propagation time is in the level-4 signal files, not here, so no delay, amplitude or quality value accompanies these rows.
Whether a given orbiter-to-lander path crosses the nucleus is a property of a shape model and is not asserted by this product.

The archived Philae position is the one known at delivery and is not updated when the localisation improves; Kofman et al. (2020, MNRAS 497, 2616) work from a position about 13 m from the archived one.

observations.meaning: Archive-published Philae lander position at each CONSERT First Science Sequence measurement point, 15468 rows of SC_POS_X/Y/Z in kilometres. This is the lander end of each sounding path; the orbiter end is the paired CN_G_O_FSS product.
limitations: The archive states the frame for these tables only in DATASET.CAT: 'The geometric data, composed of Rosetta and Philae position, velocity and attitude, are provided in the Comet Fixed Frame coordinate system.' The detached label does not repeat it.

The label's own SC_TARGET_POSITION_VECTOR and SC_SUN_POSITION_VECTOR keywords are a different frame from the table columns; DATASET.CAT gives them as Earth Mean Equator and Equinox of J2000, and the level-2 ERRATA.TXT states the label geometry keywords must not be used.
The lander position is one fixed point for the whole sequence. It is the position known at delivery, not a re-derived one; Kofman et al. (2020, MNRAS 497, 2616) work from a position about 13 m away.
This product is positions only. The CONSERT propagation time is in the level-4 signal files, not here.
Whether a given lander-to-orbiter path crosses the nucleus is a property of a shape model and is not asserted by this product.
